details.description: Gladia's real-time speech-to-text API, delivered over a WebSocket connection for live audio such as voice agents, meeting assistants and contact-center calls. A client first requests a session over REST, then streams audio to the returned WebSocket URL. It runs on Gladia's Solaria-1 model by default, covers 100+ languages with automatic language detection, and can switch the detected language mid-utterance instead of locking to the first language it hears.
advantages: Gladia states it returns partial transcripts in under 103ms, with sub-300ms end-to-end latency.
Covers 100+ languages via ISO 639-1 codes with automatic language detection.
Detects a language switch mid-utterance automatically rather than locking to the first detected language.
Supports custom vocabulary, named entity recognition and word-level timestamps for domain-specific streaming use.
Gladia reports its default Solaria-1 model returns a 37.3% word error rate on the Switchboard conversational benchmark, which it states outperforms every other provider tested.
disadvantages: Does not support speaker diarization on the live stream; Gladia's own guidance is to re-run the recording through its async API afterward for speaker labels.
Gladia's higher-accuracy Solaria-3 model is not available for real-time streaming; only Solaria-1 is used.
use_cases: Live voice agents and conversational AI
Meeting assistants and meeting copilots, using bot providers such as Recall and Meeting BaaS to capture calls

sources.title: Live transcription API reference - Gladia docs

notes: The catalog id 'real-time' names Gladia's live/streaming transcription product, not a specific 'model' value; the underlying default model is Solaria-1 per the live API docs, which also lists solaria-1 as the only option for the live 'model' parameter (solaria-3 is documented there as 'Async (pre-recorded) only'). The product/real-time page's Switchboard chart also shows a 33.9% WER bar for Solaria-3, but that figure is not used here since Solaria-3 cannot run in real time; the page's own text credits the real-time model, Solaria-1, with a 37.3% WER that it says beats every other provider, so that figure was added to advantages instead. No higher-is-better 0-100 benchmark was found, so evaluations is empty. The language count was corrected from 97+ to the 100+ the maker's page and nav both state, and the use-case list was corrected: Gladia's own integrations page names Recall and Meeting BaaS (not Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams by name) as its meeting-bot partners.
